description: The arrow control that opens a technician's daily breakdown, and the one in the table heading that opens them all, do not tell a screen reader whether they are open or closed. Their names change correctly; the open or closed state itself is never reported.
steps: Open Reports, then Technician Utilization, and set the date range to This Year.
Put a screen reader on the arrow control at the left of any technician row — Christian Pitts was used here — then open the row and listen again.

Do the same with the double-arrow control in the table heading. This was seen with the date range This Year (1 January to 6 August 2026), which returns 29 technicians, active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919, on an account that can also reach Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
current:
The names are correct and do change: "Expand Christian Pitts's daily breakdown" when closed, "Collapse Christian Pitts's daily breakdown" when open, and "Expand all technicians" / "Collapse all technicians" on the heading control.

Neither control carries the standard expanded-or-collapsed state, so a screen reader announces the name only. Both are ordinary focusable buttons, and every technician row behaves the same way.
expected: Both controls report their expanded or collapsed state to assistive technology, as well as carrying the names they already have.
source: The expand/collapse controls (per-row S4-R1 and the all-rows control S4-R4) are keyboard-focusable, toggle on Enter/Space, expose their expanded/collapsed state to assistive technology, and carry the verbatim accessible names defined in S4-R1 (per-row) and S4-R4 (all-rows).
